newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firm with futures, markets thin.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firm with futures, markets thin.

text.p: NWE gas oil was firm with futures on Monday, although traders said it was a dull day on the physical front.
On the barge market, prompt material was offered at Oct IPE +$10/+$11 fob ARA. Buyers were scarce although barges were reported to have traded at between Oct IPE +$9 and +$10.
"It's dull on the barges the German inland market appears to has been busier. Their prices seem to be higher than ours. It's usually the other way round," one barge trader said.
Traders put the lack of buyer interest down to the high premiums as well as the wide Sept/Oct spread on the IPE futures.
The October IPE contract settled at $218.25 a tonne, up $4.24, while the November contract settled at $209.75.
On cargoes, DIN talked at Oct IPE +$7.50/+$8 cif Hamburg. Traders said end-user demand was boosted by cooler temperatures.
On the low sulphur front, interest into France was reported. Premiums were steady at Oct IPE +$16/+$17 cif Le Havre.

Traders continued to speculate over the impact of North American gas oil due to hit Europe in the next two weeks. Some said its effects would be diluted by the fact that much of it does not meet European cetane specifications and will have to be reblended before use. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7714
